extra.probe: fn-3 task .1 — grok CLI surface + write-behaviour probe

isolation.mechanism: GROK_HOME, PROVEN to relocate rather than assumed: the committed capture puts HOME and GROK_HOME at DIFFERENT roots and seeds a decoy config + skill at $HOME/.grok. The contract records 0 decoy references across the mcp list and inspect probes, so GROK_HOME relocates both config and skills discovery. HOME is overridden too because the vendor-compat roots (~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/skills, ~/.cursor/skills) and ~/.agents/skills resolve from HOME, not GROK_HOME.
isolation.leader_socket: in the committed capture script, --leader-socket <nonexistent path> is appended to EVERY probe that accepts it (including the inspect probe, which is the skills-discovery oracle); the few subcommands that do not accept the flag (--version, --help, help <...>) go through grok_probe_bare. grok leader kill was never invoked.
isolation.secrets_used: none — dummy placeholders only (${HOMEPLANE_GROK_TOKEN}, ${HP_PROBE_HOST}); no real token was written anywhere
isolation.timeouts: every grok invocation in the committed capture is wrapped in a perl alarm (30-90s), including --version and the version parse; no probe ever hung or prompted.

real_home_verification.invariant: the CONFIG-BEARING surfaces of ~/.grok that a probe could touch (config.toml, skills/, hooks/) are byte-identical pre/post. This is NOT a claim of byte identity across the whole directory: ~/.grok is live.
real_home_verification.config_toml_mtime: 20:07:58, hours before the probe window opened
real_home_verification.changed_file_attribution: models_cache.json: NOT ours. Proven by re-running the isolated probes and observing its sha256 AND mtime unchanged; neither isolated home contains a models_cache.json. Attribution establishes that the probe did not cause the change - it does NOT establish byte identity of that file, which is why the whole-directory acceptance below is recorded false.
real_home_verification.whole_directory_caveat: Daniel's three grok sessions ran throughout and continuously wrote sessions/, logs/, memtrace/, active_sessions.json and models_cache.json. Exact whole-directory identity is not demonstrable without stopping his live sessions, which this task declined to do. What IS demonstrated: the probe caused none of it.

D1_skills_discovery.evidence: three disposable skills linked as symlinks into a sealed home; `grok inspect` reported directory `directory-beta-name` as its frontmatter name `frontmatter-beta-name`, and a name-less skill by its directory name `gamma-dir-name`

D2_write_mechanism.verdict: direct byte-span TOML edit of ~/.grok/config.toml (tomledit.go discipline); the `grok mcp *` CLI verbs are NOT the write path
D2_write_mechanism.entry_location: ~/.grok/config.toml, [mcp_servers.<name>] with headers in [mcp_servers.<name>.headers]; no separate store
cli_disqualifiers: drops every comment in the file (whole-document re-serialization, not a splice)
-H puts the bearer token in argv (the spec's hard constraint)
D2_write_mechanism.add_idempotency: identical re-add is byte-identical, exit 0, no duplicate
D2_write_mechanism.add_clobbers: a differing re-add replaces the entry wholesale and DELETES its headers sub-table — the writer must render the complete entry every time
D2_write_mechanism.enabled_default: true, written explicitly; no `grok mcp enable` step needed
D2_write_mechanism.backup_restore: byte-level restore is sufficient — no state outside the file is touched
D2_write_mechanism.list_caveat: `grok mcp list` covers the TOML scopes only, NOT everything grok loads (see compat finding); `grok mcp list --json` also echoes header values verbatim
D2_write_mechanism.doctor_exit_code: 1 when any server is unhealthy; JSON on stdout, unstructured tracing ERROR on stderr (the capture records the two streams separately)

D3_token_custody.verdict: inline bearer in [mcp_servers.homeplane.headers] Authorization, in a config Homeplane forces to 0600; NO environment indirection
D3_token_custody.env_indirection_available: yes for url (OBSERVED); documented upstream for all [mcp_servers.*] strings
D3_token_custody.env_indirection_form: ${VAR} / ${VAR:-default} in any [mcp_servers.*] string, stored verbatim and expanded at load time
D3_token_custody.env_indirection_proof: url: OBSERVED both ways - `https://${HP_PROBE_HOST}/mcp` reported target as the literal placeholder unset, and as https://expanded.example.invalid/mcp set. headers: only that a ${VAR} placeholder is STORED verbatim; an expanded Authorization header arriving at a server is NOT independently observed here.
D3_token_custody.env_indirection_rejected_because: fn-1 already recorded and tested this in codex_token_test.go — env indirection works only in a process that inherited the exporting shell, and Homeplane does not launch grok
D3_token_custody.containment: ~/.grok/config.toml is outside every repo; passes resolved-symlink + git check-ignore containment as ~/.codex/config.toml does
D3_token_custody.mode_durability: NOT durable — the file is 0644 today and `grok mcp add` resets 0600 to 0644; Homeplane must set and re-assert 0600 on every apply
D3_token_custody.header_expansion_gap: an end-to-end probe against a local endpoint was attempted and abandoned - grok's streamable-HTTP client would not handshake with a stub cheap enough to keep in a capture script, and each re-capture paid minutes of retry. The gap changes NO decision: D3 rejects env indirection for any field, so header expansion is not load-bearing. A future task wanting to rely on it must observe it first.

leader_process.verdict: no resident leader exists; config is read fresh from disk per invocation
leader_process.spec_premise_corrected: the spec asserted ~/.grok/leader.sock exists — it does NOT, and no socket of any kind is present, despite three live grok sessions
leader_process.leader_list_output: No leader candidates found (both the real home and a sealed one)
leader_process.staleness: an entry added by one invocation was visible to the very next invocation; no restart or refresh step
leader_process.fresh_process_contract: pass --leader-socket <nonexistent path> so the invocation is fresh BY CONSTRUCTION; assert `grok leader list` finds no candidates and record it; never call `grok leader kill` (it would stop Daniel's sessions)

findings_resolved_by_daniel.severity: blocks R5, corrupts R3 audit identity, engages the R12 falsification gate
findings_resolved_by_daniel.observed: grok's default [compat.claude] mcps = true makes it load ~/.claude.json; `grok inspect` on this machine already reports homeplane (http), gno (stdio) and rize (http) with origin `~/.claude.json [claude]`
findings_resolved_by_daniel.consequence: grok can reach the Homeplane edge TODAY under Claude Code's bearer token and grant identity, before any fn-3 work. Revoking grok's grant would not cut grok's access (R5 could not produce a real denied call), and calls would be audited under Claude Code's grant (R3).
findings_resolved_by_daniel.mitigation_partial: merge precedence is config.toml > claude > cursor, so a grok entry named EXACTLY `homeplane` shadows the inherited one — name agreement is load-bearing, not cosmetic
options: rely on name shadowing alone (no extra writes, but any non-shadowed Claude server still loads and the guarantee depends on names never diverging)
write [compat.claude] mcps = false into grok's config (makes grok's connector access exclusively its own grant, but changes Daniel's general grok behaviour beyond Homeplane's own entries)
findings_resolved_by_daniel.recommendation: the second, scoped and explicit — but it is Daniel's call and task .2 must not assume it
findings_resolved_by_daniel.note: the same default also makes grok discover Claude's skills including the vault-authored homeplane-capabilities; that is likely desirable and should be left on

capture_script_fail_closed.problem_fixed: the capture recorded probe exit statuses and always returned success, so a failed/timed-out/empty probe was written up as a passing observation
measures: expect_ok / expect_rc after every probe (exact status, not merely non-zero)
reject_timeout: exit 142 (128+SIGALRM) is refused everywhere, including on probes expected to fail - a killed probe is not a fast non-interactive failure
relocation gate requires POSITIVE sentinels (entries and skills written to the relocated dir present in the same output) before decoy absence counts
probe exit status passed through a file so it survives $(...) subshell capture
doctor stdout validated as parseable JSON rather than asserted to be
capture written to a temp file and atomically renamed only after validation, so a transient failure cannot destroy the last known-good contract
capture_script_fail_closed.tests: internal/agent/harness/capture_script_test.go drives the real script against stub groks: probe failure, early help failure, timed-out probe, probes that succeed but report nothing, no partial file left behind, and an existing contract left byte-identical after a failed recapture
